# BlightBloom — Phase 2 project cleanup audit

2026-10-31. **Proposal only. No cleanup authorized by this document.** Sole output: this new report. No existing files, scenes, prefabs, sources, scripts, settings or Git configuration/history were modified by the audit. No Unity/Blender launch, reimport, gameplay validation, package installation, compression, move, deletion, commit or push. Phase 1 external cache cleanup is not repeated.

## 1. Executive findings and recoverable storage

- Available at measurement: **2.473 GB**. Project: **17.881 GB logical / 18.004 GB allocated**, 43412 regular files. GB is decimal; APFS/clones/snapshots and background writers can change physical recovery.
- **ARCHIVE: 88 exact files, 2.148 GB logical / 2.148 GB allocated.** These are mainly rejected/intermediate exterior work plus six historical comparison scenes. This is recoverable only after a verified separate backup and explicit authorization; without external storage it is not immediate free space.
- **DELETE CANDIDATE: 9 exact files, 84,004 logical bytes / 110,592 allocated bytes.** Only regenerable Finder `.DS_Store` view metadata meets the conservative no-required-dependency threshold. No architectural, character, material, texture, gameplay or shader file is verified disposable.
- **Git savings from deleting working files: 0 counted.** Git itself remains protected. No Library, Temp, Logs or cache deletion is proposed in this phase.
- Most non-Production02 assets still have reusable-kit, review-scene, source-art or tooling value. No broad asset-library purge is justified. Missing a static reference is not proof of disposability.

## 3. Dependency method, coverage and limits

Enumerated the entire ArtSource and Assets trees and read all available relevant C#, Blender Python, shader and serialized/text documentation files. Parsed Unity `.meta` GUIDs, serialized references in scenes/prefabs/materials/controllers/assets/importers and ProjectSettings; followed dependencies from all **21 scenes** and Production02 (**306 resolved Assets paths**, including inactive objects/prefabs). Exact filename/path mentions in processing scripts and documentation are distinguished from serialized dependencies. Code inspection also accounts for Editor menu items, automatic initialization, C# type references/reflection, path-based loads, shader names and Python import/exec dependencies.

This is a static repository audit, not a live AssetDatabase or runtime reachability proof. Computed path strings, binary Blender links/packed images, FBX embedded dependencies, arbitrary external calls and reflection cannot be ruled out exhaustively. Such uncertainty yields KEEP, never DELETE CANDIDATE. No Blender file was loaded or saved and no geometry-duplicate conclusion is inferred from file names. Hash checks compare bytes only; embedded repeated source collections may contain identical geometry but require a separately authorized Blender datablock audit to deduplicate safely.

Python syntax parsing exceptions: 0. Symlink files were not followed (0 observed across project). Exact file/hash candidate inventories below are snapshots, not deletion authority. The new report is excluded from its own inventory/savings. Metadata retains its owner’s classification; directory `.meta` files remain KEEP.

## 4. Essential scenes, assets and active systems

- KEEP Production02, StyledDetails07, UsabilityBlockout01 and the currently recorded exterior development scene. The latter is shown in `Library/LastSceneManagerSetup.txt`; this is a saved Editor-state observation, not live UI inspection.
- KEEP all six approved architecture/botanical kit libraries, signage/lantern assets, reusable prefabs and source artwork. Keep current Locomotion03 rig/FBX/Animator/driver and its predecessor prefabs/scripts: serialized references persist even when an instance is disabled.
- KEEP door `Assets/BlightBloom/Prototypes/CrookedMortarUsability01/BlockoutDoor.cs` and scene-local `.../CrookedMortarProduction02/Production02StairOrbitCamera.cs`: both are directly referenced by Production02/review scenes despite their folder names.
- KEEP controller/input/orbit scripts; Editor builders remain menu entry points. Tutorial `ReadmeEditor.cs` has InitializeOnLoad and reflection: unreferenced by a scene is irrelevant.
- KEEP `Assets/Scenes/SampleScene.unity`: it is still the enabled scene in `ProjectSettings/EditorBuildSettings.asset`. Choosing a future build scene is a separate decision, not cleanup.
- KEEP original Tripo GLBs at `ArtSource/Blender/Architecture/CrookedMortar/TripoImports/storybook cottage 3d model.glb` and `ArtSource/Blender/Interiors/CrookedMortar/TripoImports/rustic wooden cabinet 3d model.glb`. They are not in the Exteriors import tree.
- KEEP approved exterior OriginalReference, RepairedHigh, Optimized sources and their distinct previous-save backups; both boundary-map sources, uncut safety reference, final TerrainSeparated01 candidate, closure textures and authoritative validation data. Do not substitute Stage/WORKING/rejected files for the final candidate.

Important source-side chain: `verify_final_copy.py` reads helper code from BoundaryMapping01/create_boundary_map.py via text extraction/exec, plus BoundaryMapping02 reference, Topology.npz and final candidate. Thus an older boundary-generation script is still part of final validation. Stage01–05 depend on one another through computed names; SafeSeparated closure/repair scripts read their paired Blender checkpoints. `sample_foundation.py` reads WORKING and generates recorded texture copies. New final capture scripts do not erase those reproducibility relationships. Reusable capture/validation utilities are not junk simply because the latest validation already passed.

Future, separately approved policy: evaluate Git LFS for deliberately tracked `.blend`, `.fbx`, `.glb` and large painted-source binaries. LFS requires installed tooling, hosting/quota/credentials and collaborators able to fetch; none were installed or configured here. Tracking future files does not shrink existing Git history, and local LFS storage can still consume space. Existing-history migration would rewrite history and is NOT proposed as this cleanup. Prefer a curated set of approved editable sources plus verified external archival of rejected snapshots, and avoid repeatedly checkpointing generated intermediate binaries once a separately approved policy exists. Auxiliary snapshot storage needs its own documented retention decision; never manually delete objects. Working-file removal gives **zero immediate Git-history savings**.

## 10. Cleanup order and human decisions

1. Preserve all current source and confirm the pending standalone Unity export first; no cleanup should remove its final source, textures, validation helpers or boundaries.
2. If desired, approve only the tiny exact Finder metadata deletion list; expect negligible headroom.
3. Select a verified archive destination and archive the documented terrain intermediates/rejected experiments as restorable cohorts. Check hashes and dependencies again before any later local removal. With no separate backup, retain them.
4. Decide whether the six older comparison scenes are still artistically needed. Archive scene/meta and its source/tool context together; do not delete underlying shared modules.
5. Review cabinet/character legacy variants, no-incoming-GUID assets, computed-path tools and .blend1 backup policy manually. They remain KEEP until usage/lineage is settled.
6. Consider future binary-versioning policy separately. Do not include Git or Library recovery in any source cleanup estimate.
